Hi Alice / Priyom / Ops team —

Thanks for the clear summary — wanted to share a concise, technical take you can use to evaluate options quickly. High level first, then recommended next steps.

Short answer: Dedicated reserved capacity is the right first step if you need predictable tail latency and compute/network isolation during peak promotions. Private VPC provides additional network/egress controls and a private control plane if your security policies require it. Hosted (shared) gives fastest time-to-value but can exhibit variable p99 under noisy neighbor events; we can mitigate this with caching, batching, and fallback models, but predictability is weaker than Dedicated.

Key details:
- Noisy-neighbor impact (shared pools): in our customer load tests, an aggressive co-tenant workload can increase p99 by ~40–150ms depending on model size and request mix. Smaller/lightweight models typically see lower delta (~40–60ms); large context/stateful workloads (long seq lengths/large KV cache pressure) can push the delta to the higher end.
- Dedicated isolation: Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools (no compute contention) and separate KV cache allocation. Network egress still traverses our control plane unless you choose Private VPC; for most customers Dedicated reduces p99 variability to within ~10–30ms of baseline. We operate Dedicated with a per-deployment p99 SLO that we tune by model profile — typical internal target: p99 < 120ms for classification/embedding-style workloads with sustained throughput within provisioned capacity.
- Private VPC / on-prem: adds customer-managed networking and optional on-prem control plane. This removes shared-control-plane egress concerns and can satisfy strict egress/compliance requirements. Latency profile is comparable to Dedicated but requires more onboarding time and infra coordination.
- Autoscaling & burst: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and short-duration burst capacity; we size burst pools to handle short spikes (you can set a burst window and protection levels). For a 600 req/s peak we typically recommend a base reservation for sustained load and burst capacity for short promos.
- Mitigations on Hosted: prefix/KV caching, continuous batching, and model quantization can reduce per-token compute and significantly lower p99 in practice. If you opt to stay on Hosted initially, we recommend a strict SLO/error-budget for tail latency and a scheduled ramp test.

Recommended next steps:
1) Technical scoping call (30–45m) with your ops/infra and our runtime engineering to pick candidate model(s) for a dedicated trial.
2) 72-hour Dedicated trial: run your workload with our reserved pool + a 2-hour sustained load window and multiple promo spikes to measure real p50/p95/p99 under representative traffic.
3) Define SLOs and an error budget: e.g., target p99 <= 120ms with an error budget allowing X% of minutes/month to exceed (we can propose values).
4) If egress or audit controls are required, we can scope Private VPC as the follow-up after trial results.
